title: From Gin's Book. The Six Abilities

blocks.p: For the next few days the sparks kept coming, each one weaker than the last, and each time one fired Rei went back to Gin's book and found the chapter Gin had written about it. Gin had written all six, path by path, in his patient field voice, as if he had known someone would one day need them in a hurry. Rei read them on the train, at the konbini counter, in the bath. He read them the way a man reads the instructions for a machine that has already started.

doc.title: Clairsentience. The noise problem
lines: Reading requires opening. When you open to read, you can be read.

Telepathy reads minds. Clairsentience reads the space around minds. A Clairsentient knows you are angry. A Telepath knows why. A Clairsentient reads the surface of the lake. A Telepath goes into the water.

Low cost for each use, high cost over years. Unmanaged practitioners with several channels half open produce static. To an assessor it feels loud, everywhere at once. The rank gets recorded at the floor of what could be read.
This is our family's path. It is the one Rei calls instinct. G.U.

doc.title: Telepathy. The push and the open
lines: Clairsentience is eavesdropping. Telepathy is a conversation the other party may not know they are having.
There is no 'I accidentally read you' defence. Every read is a choice.
Thoughts are not language. It is interpretation, not recording.
At the deepest levels it is the only path that can enter a partly possessed practitioner's mind. The difference between a recovery that finds the host and one that finds only the demon.
A telepath is the only person in every room who cannot pretend they did not notice. G.U.

doc.title: Psychometabolism. The cost of being the medic
lines: It works where the body meets the veil. It reads injury, stability, depletion.
Moving stability from yourself to another person is inefficient. You lose more than they gain. You cannot fully heal yourself.
Teams treat the medic as infrastructure. The Grid runs them in pairs. The CVD uses one at a time and wonders why they leave.
It is not a risk. It is the bill, and it always comes. G.U.

doc.title: Telekinesis. Visibility
lines: Force, and then architecture. At the start you push. Later you build with what is already in the room.
It leaves signatures. A careful small use lasts half an hour. Real force lasts hours. Combat lasts days.
Telekinetics learn to hide young, the first time a cup moves with someone in the room. Half the operatives wearing suppression marks chose them.
A cup moved in our kitchen in the night. Two centimetres to the left. I did not move it. The cup is still where it moved to. G.U.

doc.title: Psychokinesis. The noise ceiling
lines: Electrical, thermal, sonic, membrane. Manipulation first. Generation later.
Every use in the city leaves evidence. A dead camera leaves an event log. A surge leaves a power record.
Warmth and cold are the quiet tools. They leave nothing on a screen.
A practitioner who can hurt the formless can hurt anything.
The hallway lights flickered. Third time this week. I am not a Psychokinesis practitioner. My secondary is something else. G.U.

doc.title: Teleportation. The destination problem
lines: The rarest after Telepathy. You need line of sight, or a clear remembered image, or a live description. A demolished building goes wrong in specific and unpleasant ways.
Transit runs through the Threshold. Possession in mid-transit is documented.
A passenger doubles the cost. A conscious person who resists cannot be carried. The target's will decides.
I came back from a pocket three districts off in 2013, six hours late, and dreamed for a month that I had not come back at all.
I have caught myself mapping the exits from my brother's kitchen. G.U.

blocks.p: It was the last page that Rei read most often. It was not in Gin's voice. It was a reference sheet Gin had copied out by hand from somewhere he should not have been, and he had underlined one word three times.

doc.title: Opening a New Path. Development Rules
lines: A practitioner cannot open a new ability path alone. Readiness can build, but the opening needs direct transmission from someone who already walks that path. Not instruction. Transmission. The teacher uses the ability close to the student, again and again, until something in the student's aperture recognises what it has been reaching toward, and opens.
The teacher must have the path. Not training in it. Having it. This is why masters matter.
Sessions needed. Sensitive, eight to ten. Ritualist, six to eight. Channel, four to six. Arbiter, two to four. Vanguard and above, one or two. At that height it is recognition, not development.
A session is a real scene with stakes. Interrupted training does not count. Practice under threat counts double.
The opening comes at a moment of recognition, not on a schedule.

Exception. The Uedera are born with two paths open, not one. The second does not need a teacher. It sits dormant from birth and opens through a recognition event, when it is needed and reached for without knowing. This is why Gin presented as single-path for years.
Gin, in the margin. The Uedera line opens faster than the rule says. Half again as fast. I have not told Rei.

blocks.p: By the fourth day the sparks had almost stopped. The teleport flicker never came back after the second night. The lamp hum faded. The old woman's thoughts went quiet behind the wall. Rei understood why from the underlined word. He had not been taught anything. He had touched a man with every path lit and come home warm from it, and the warmth was cooling, the way a hand cools after it lets go of another hand. The sparks would not stay unless someone who truly had the path sat beside him and used it, again and again, until his aperture recognised what it had felt. They could be taught now. That was all.

The grain under them did not fade. Every morning he turned his palms up in the light from the kitchen window and found the second set of prints exactly where it had been, a little clearer, a little more his.
